articleTitle: End-fire phased array 5G antenna design using leaf-shaped bow-tie elements for 28/38 GHz MIMO applications
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, a new design of mm-Wave phased array 5G antenna for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) applications has been introduced. Two identical linear phased arrays with eight leaf-shaped bow-tie antenna elements have been used at different sides of the mobile-phone PCB. An Arlon AR 350 dielectric with properties of h=0.5 mm, ε=3.5, and δ=0.0026 has been used as a substrate of the proposed design. The antenna is working in the frequency range of 25 to 40 GHz (more than 45% FBW) and can be easily fit into current handheld devices. The proposed MIMO antenna has good radiation performances at 28 and 38 GHz which both are powerful candidates to be the carrier frequency of the future 5G cellular networks.

articleTitle: UWB MM-Wave antenna array with quasi omnidirectional beams for 5G handheld devices
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: An ultra-wideband (UWB) millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) dipole antenna array for fifth generation (5G) communications is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna is working in the frequency range of 23-33 GHz (10 GHz bandwidth with more than 35% FBW). Ten compact UWB dipole antenna elements designed on a Rogers RT5880 substrate have been deployed along the edge region of the cell phone PCB. The feature of compact design with UWB characteristic makes them well-suited for 5G cellular devices such as laptops, tablets, mobile phones etc. Input impedance and radiation properties of the proposed antenna array have been discussed. The antenna features quasi-omnidirectional radiation beams at different scanning angles.

articleTitle: Novel square/rectangle waveguide septum polarizer
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A new square/rectangle waveguide septum polarizer is proposed. The septum is composed of a tapered slot energy collector in the square waveguide part and a slot radiator in the common side of the two rectangle waveguide feeders. Samples were designed, fabricated and measured. Both the simulated data (HFSS) and the experimental data are given to verify the performance. As a result, the 4-port S-parameters show the proposed structure has good performances in the return losses, insertion losses and phase difference.

articleTitle: A miniaturized directional coupler with high isolation for RFID reader
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A novel, low-cost miniaturized directional coupler with high isolation is presented in this paper. The proposed coupler is obtained by using a short stub on the coupled port of a conventional branch-line directional coupler to achieve a very high isolation. Meanwhile, for the demand of miniaturization and low-cost of RFID systems, transmission lines are equivalent to the “π” lumped-element networks, and the GaAs-IPD (Gallium Arsenide Based Integrated Passive Device) technology is used to implement the physical layout of the proposed coupler. Simulation results indicate that the directional coupler, with a high isolation of 60.1dB and a size of 2.49mm×3.60mm, can satisfy the required RFID reader specifications at 2.45GHz.

articleTitle: Computationally efficient sparse Bayesian learning via generalized approximate message passing
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: The sparse Bayesian learning (also referred to as Bayesian compressed sensing) algorithm is a popular approach for sparse signal recovery, and has demonstrated superior performance in several experiments. Nevertheless, the sparse Bayesian learning algorithm has a computational complexity that grows rapidly with the dimension of the signal, which hinders its application to many practical problems even with moderately large data sets. To address this issue, in this paper, we propose a computationally efficient sparse Bayesian learning method by integrating the generalized approximate message passing (GAMP) technique. Specifically, the algorithm is developed within an expectation-maximization (EM) framework, using the GAMP to efficiently compute an approximation of the posterior distribution of hidden variables. The hyperparameters associated with the hierarchical Gaussian prior are learned by iteratively maximizing the Q-function which is calculated based on the posterior approximation obtained from the GAMP. Numerical results are provided to illustrate the computational efficiency and the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: User scheduling and cluster formation in fog computing based radio access networks
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Fog computing based radio access networks (FRANs) are potential paradigms for further improving throughput and decreasing latency. By fully utilizing the caching and signal processing capabilities of fog computing based access points (FAPs), the burden on the fronthaul can be alleviated. However, when the spectrum is shared among FAPs, the inter-FAP interference can be severe, which degrades the performance of F-RANs. In this paper, to mitigate inter-FAP interference, a distributed cluster formation algorithm is proposed, which considers the fronthaul cost induced by fetching contents missed in the cache. Meanwhile, a distributed user scheduling algorithm is designed to help each FAP schedules the proper user, aiming at optimizing the system throughput. By simulations, the benefit of enabling caching is validated, and the effectiveness of the proposed scheduling algorithm is shown.

articleTitle: Frequency estimation algorithm for ranging of millimeter wave LFMCW radar
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of ranging algorithm for millimeter wave linear frequency modulated continuous wave (LFMCW) radar, The modified Rife algorithm (M-Rife) is investigated in this paper. To decrease the error results from low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), a frequency estimation algorithm based on the fast Fourier transform (FFT) coefficient is proposed. The FFT coefficient is used to decide the frequency shift direction. Simulation results show that the method based on FFT coefficient has higher estimation precision on the measured frequency band and better performance in the case of low SNR.

articleTitle: A combination of VLC and WiFi based indoor wireless access network and its handover strategy
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Visible Light Communication (VLC) has many advantages such as high-speed data transmission and non-frequency authorization, which provided a good solution for indoor access environment with an effective and energy-saving way. This paper proposes a combination VLC + WiFi based indoor wireless access network structure. Different network architectures are analyzed and optimal scheme is given. Based on the numerical calculation, the handover model is introduced. Finally, a demo system is designed and implemented.

articleTitle: Using UWB IR radar technology to decode multiple chipless RFID tags
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, a technique to decode multiple ultra-wide band (UWB) chipless radio frequency identification (RFID) tags using UWB impulse radio (IR) radar technology is proposed. The methodology presented is proven for decoding several chipless RFID tags simultaneously placed in the reader's identification zone, and it is based on the analysis of the received pulses backscattered from chipless tags located at the same or different distance from the radar. The decoding takes places using an algorithm that analyzes the backscattered pulses time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA), energy and the chipless tags coding to detect tags-collision scenarios. Several chipless tags having either the same or different code within the UWB frequency range from 4 to 8 GHz are fabricated using aluminum on polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrate. The technique is validated experimentally using the UWB IR radar principle and technology to perform the decoding of multiple chipless RFID tags simultaneously placed in reader's identification zone. The chipless RFID tags are successfully decoded in eight different combinations scenarios.

articleTitle: Social-aware content downloading for fog radio access networks supported device-to-device communications
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Social-aware device-to-device (D2D) communications are seen as promising solutions to satisfy the emerging demand for popular content sharing. In this paper, social relationship strength is considered in a fog radio access network (FRAN) supported D2D communications, which facilitates content sharing among mobile users. Then a non-convex optimization problem of joint content downloading mode selection, beam-forming design, and power control is formulated, aiming at maximizing system utility related to both throughput and social relationship strength. To solve the problem, a branch and bound and weighted minimum mean square error based algorithm is proposed. Simulation results show that the F-RAN with social-aware D2D can effectively improve the overall throughput and alleviate the burden of fronthaul.

articleTitle: K band low power voltage controlled oscillator using 180 nm CMOS technology with a new high quality inductor
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Low power K-band voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) using 180nm CMOS technology is presented in this paper. The proposed VCO achieves a wide tuning range from 21.4 to 25.16 GHz by using switched capacitors. The performance of proposed VCO (phase noise, output power and DC power consumption) is improved by designing a new high quality factor inductor that has a shape of figure of eight in 0.18 μm CMOS technology, the quality factor of the proposed inductor is 20.8 at the frequency of interest. Two NMOS switching capacitors to select one of four different frequency. The VCO core consumes 2.7 mA from a power supply of 1.1 V. From the post layout simulation the proposed VCO achieves a wide-frequency tuning range of 21.4-25.16 GHz (16.15%), and a good phase noise of -99 dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset from 25.16 GHz carrier frequency. The calculated figure of merit (FoM) and FoM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub> of this VCO are -183 dBc/Hz and -187 dBc/Hz.

articleTitle: User-centric view of smart attacks in wireless networks
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: By applying smart and programmable radio devices, selfish end-users can launch smart attacks and choose multiple types of attacks such as jamming and eavesdropping according to the ongoing transmission of wireless networks. In this paper, we apply prospect theory (PT) to formulate the interaction between a smart attacker as an end-user who makes subjective decision regarding his or her attack mode under uncertain attack detection accuracy and a mobile user who chooses whether or not to apply the higher-layer security mechanism to enhance the physical (PHY)-layer security mechanism as a zero-sum game. The Nash equilibria (NEs) of the static smart attack game are derived and their existence conditions are provided to study the impact of the subjectivity of smart attackers. We also propose a defense strategy based on Q-learning, a model free reinforcement learning technique against subjective smart attacks in the dynamic game. Simulation results show that the proposed defense strategy can exploit the subjective view of smart attackers to suppress the attack motivation of end-users and improve the utility of the mobile user.

articleTitle: A tunable bandpass-to-bandstop filter using PIN diode
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A tunable bandpass-to-bandstop filter using PIN diode is proposed in this paper. The proposed filter employs two quarter-wavelength resonators and a half-wavelength resonator with six varactors and a PIN diode. The bandpass-to-bandstop transformation can be achieved by adjusting the PIN diode. The center frequency of the proposed filter can be flexibly controlled by adjusting the bias voltage of the four varactors at the end of resonators. By adjusting two varactors connected to feeding line, external quality factors can be flexibly controlled. So the proposed bandpass filter can be designed conveniently. In the bandpass mode, a tuning range of 650-1200 MHz (59.5%) with return loss better than 15 dB can be achieved. In the bandstop mode, a tuning range of 675-1200 MHz (57.5%) can be achieved. The rejection level of the bandstop mode is higher than 15 dB.

articleTitle: Indoor detection and tracking of human targets with UWB radar sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, the whole signal processing chain for an ultra-wideband (UWB) radar sensor network (RSN) is presented, starting from real measurements collected by sensor devices, and ending with the estimation of the target trajectory. The RSN is composed by one transmitter and six receivers, and monitors an indoor area of about 70 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> performing tracking of a human target. The proposed processing chain consists of: clutter removal, a novel detection scheme, one-dimensional clustering, trilateration, two-dimensional clustering, particle-based probability hypothesis density filter tracking, and data association. Numerical results show the remarkable performance of the system, resulting in a root mean square localization error of 36 cm, a value smaller than the target size. The presented experimental study show that it is possible to accurately track human targets using a UWB RSN in a densely cluttered environment.

articleTitle: Potentiality of a bi-directional system based on 60GHz and VLC technologies for e-health applications
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: To support the E-HEALTH services, a locatable, radiation-free and high-capacity communication system is urgently needed in Hospitals. In this paper, a bi-directional system is proposed combining 60GHz technology for the uplink communications and VLC downlink communications in order to offer new services of HD files as well as indoor localization. Meanwhile, state-of-the-art localization techniques based on mmW will be presented.

articleTitle: Design of low phase noise substrate integrated waveguide oscillator based on complexquality factor (Qsc)
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A low phase noise substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) oscillator based on complex quality factor (Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</sub>) is presented. The oscillator employing a fourth-degree cross-coupled bandpass SIW filter is designed at the oscillation frequency for the feedback loop as a frequency stabilization element. In this paper, the peak frequency of the complex quality factor (Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</sub>) is adopted for oscillator design instead of designing the oscillator at groupdelay peak frequency conventionally. The measured phase noise performance of the developed oscillator is -141.4 dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset frequency with the figure of merit (FOM) of -198.3dBc/Hz.

articleTitle: Conceptual design of a dual-band circularly polarized antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A novel, dual-band circularly polarized (CP) antenna is proposed and numerically investigated in this paper. The operation mechanism of the antenna is analyzed and design guidelines are laid down in the beginning. Then, a combined dipole antenna is designed and demonstrated to exhibit a dual-band circularly polarized characteristic. The antenna is composed of a planar magnetic dipole and a square loop. Preliminary simulated results are presented to validate the theoretical analysis. The proposed design approach in this work can be potentially applied in the development of dual-band CP antennas for various wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Study on the multipath propagation characteristics of UWB signal for indoor lab environments
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: The propagation characteristics of ultra-wideband (UWB) signal have been a popular topic in wireless communications with the advantages of large bandwidth and high communication rate. This paper studies on the multipath propagation characteristics of UWB signal for indoor laboratory environment by time domain ray tracing method. Also, reflection, diffraction, transmission and direct rays are all considered. Firstly, the validity of simulation based on time domain ray tracing method is proved. Then, in order to research on the multipath propagation characteristics, the root-mean-square (RMS) delay spread and path loss are analyzed by simulation. Later, the study can provide the theoretical basis for wireless communication network coverage and optimization of UWB signal in indoor environments.

articleTitle: 26/40 GHz CMOS VCOs design of radio front-end for 5G mobile devices
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a radio front end for future 5G mobile devices and present the design and verification of two fundamental voltage-controlled oscillators (VCO) working at potential 5G carrier frequencies. Based on two types of very small on-chip inductors with high quality factor, two LC-VCOs are fabricated and tested in a 130nm CMOS process. With a C-shaped on-chip inductor, VCO 1 achieves a frequency range from 25.23 to 27 GHz, while VCO 2 can be continuously tuned from 39.6 to 41.8 GHz by using a very small horseshoe-shaped on-chip inductor. The measured phase noise for VCO 1 and VCO 2 are -101.9 dBc/Hz and -94.8 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz frequency offset when working at 25.58 GHz and 41.81 GHz respectively, which correspond to FOM of -176.7 dBc/Hz and -172.1 dBc/Hz.

articleTitle: Design of broadband power amplifier based on ADS
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: With the development of wireless communication technology, the research process of RF power amplifier (RFPA) is promoted greatly. This paper presents the design and measurements of a broadband LDMOS RF power amplifier. The power amplifier adopts Source-Pull and Load-Pull to design the input and output matching circuits. And ADS is used to optimize and simulate the circuits. The frequency of the power amplifier is 945MHz, the measured output power is 45 W and efficiency is 42% with 1 W input power. Moreover, the maximum power added efficiency (PAE) is about 57% and the gain compression is 0.73dB.

articleTitle: Max-min fair harvested energy based beamforming designs for MISO SWIPT secrecy system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: We investigate beamfoming design in a multiple-input-single-output (MISO) secrecy system with simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT). Our aim is to maximize the minimum harvested energy among multiple energy harvesting (EH) receiver subject to the secrecy rate constraint and the total transmit power constraint. In order to avoid the performance loss resulted from the rank relaxation, we propose a novel iterative method to obtain the near-optimal beamforming vector. Considering the perfect channel statement information (CSI) scenario, we propose a successive convex approximation (SCA) iterative algorithm based on Taylor series approximation. Simulation results are provided to validate the performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Positioning algorithm for wireless capsule endoscopy based on RSS
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A large quantity of disorders that occur in the gastrointestinal tract have always been challenging to be diagnosed in a complex environment inside the human body, but with the invention and development of wireless capsule endoscope. Many patients that experienced traditional treatment will perceive stupendous convenience. Such wireless capsule endoscope requires a highly accurate localization system. The paper presents a positioning algorithm of internal the human body's capsule endoscope. The idea is to measure electromagnetic power by the capsule emitted that through the human body, and positioning the exact location of the capsule endoscope. The algorithm has been developed and simulated on MAT LAB. Simulation results demonstrate it's highly accurateness.

articleTitle: SARS: A novel QoE based service-aware resource scheduling scheme in wireless network
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel QoE based service-aware resource scheduling scheme for multi-mode wireless terminals in the wireless access network, the virtualization of radio access network leads to various virtual bus to offer efficient bandwidth resource for the media terminal to reach best of user experience, especially for the different popular level online streaming video. The quality of experience evaluation system is evolved beyond the QoS level, which means a new customer-centered network epoch. A SARS model is proposed that SARS server makes an optimized virtualization of the SGWs to VBs, so the MT can achieve both more wireless bandwidth and more satisfaction degree, which is shown in the simulation result for the different users groups.

articleTitle: A wide axial-ratio beamwidth circularly polarized microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A circularly polarized (CP) microstrip antenna with wide axial-ratio beamwidth is presented for global navigation satellite systems. Four unequal 90° sectors are truncated symmetrically at four corners of a square patch and four slits along the orthogonal axes are cut on the patch for CP radiation and compact antenna size. The 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of the proposed antenna is 16.0 MHz (1.566-1.582 GHz) with a 3-dB AR beamwidth around 170° within the bandwidth and the 10-dB return loss bandwidth is 64.0 MHz (1.543-1.607 GHz). The overall size of the antenna is 0.368 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.368 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.011 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>.

articleTitle: Reduced-order root-MUSIC based on Schur spectral factorization
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: The root multiple signal classification (Root-MUSIC) has recently drawn a considerable attention, by using a polynomial rooting instead of spectral searching to reduce the complexity. The Root-MUSIC is computationally efficient in conjunction with a uniform linear array (ULA) composed of M sensors. Compared with traditional multiple signal classification (MUISC) algorithm, Root-MUSIC is more advantaged but also has a redundancy by solving a (2M-2) order polynomial. The polynomial is intensely complex when large number of sensors is used, and consequently, tremendous computations are required. A reduced-order Root-MUSIC based on the Schur spectral factorization is presented in this paper, which only need to calculate a (M-1) order polynomial. Simulations are conducted to support the validity of the algorithm. The results show that reduced-order Root-MUSIC has a similar root mean square error (RMSE) performance as Root-MUSIC with less computation.

articleTitle: Wideband Fabry-Pérot resonator for 28 GHz applications
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, a compact design of Fabry-Pérot (FP) resonator for 28 GHz applications is proposed. The antenna is composed of a coaxial-fed source radiator (patch antenna), an air cavity, and a partially reflecting surface (PRS) with 4×4 array of cells. The antenna has a good radiation behavior in the desired operation band of 26-30 GHz with 6 dBi directivity improvement. The antenna is designed on low-cost FR-4 dielectrics (h=0.8 mm, ε=4.3, and δ=0.025). The designed FP resonator exhibits wide bandwidth around 28 GHz which is one the candidate bands for the future fifth generation (5G) wireless systems. It exhibits a high-gain directive-beam pattern in the broadside direction with 12 dBi directivity at 28 GHz. The antenna has a compact size of 25×25 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A balanced bandpass filter with two transmission zeros based on square patch resonators
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Inspired by the excellent properties of a patch element, the square patch resonator is considered for the implementation of a balanced bandpass filter with two transmission zeros. Two square patch resonators with proper port location are cascaded for the realization of dual mode differential bandpass filtering characteristics. By adding open stubs and spur-lines to the basic configuration, a balanced bandpass filter with good differential-mode selectivity and good common-mode rejection can be implemented. For demonstration, a balanced bandpass filter operating at 2.4 GHz is designed, fabricated and measured. A reasonable agreement between simulation and measurement can be found.

articleTitle: Compact printed ultra-wide band filter employing SRR-DGS
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A topology of compact planar microstrip ultra-wideband (UWB) bandpass filter (BPF) has been proposed and implemented in this paper. By employing split-ring resonator defected ground structure (SRR DGS), the BPF with good selectivity and out-of-band characteristics are obtained. U-slot DGS is also used to improve high frequency suppression. Simulated results are confirmed via experiment, showing good wideband filtering performance. The measured insertion loss is less than 1.6 dB, the return loss is more than 15 dB, and the variation of group delay is less than 0.5 ns throughout the most of pass band with suppression about 15dB in 11 GHz-20GHz.

articleTitle: UWB frequency selective surfaces with angular stability and notched band at 5.5 GHz
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, new ultra-wideband (UWB) stopband frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) are proposed. The frequency band, over which a flat stopband is achieved, covers the entire UWB band. The proposed FSS constitutes with compact size unit cells sandwiched in between two dielectric substrates. In addition, the performance of the proposed FSS is stable over a wide range of incident angles for TE and TM polarizations. In order to avoid the interference with WLAN applications that share a part of the UWB band, a notched band is realized at 5.5 GHz. Providing good candidates for UWB applications and an optimized solution for integration with compact broadband circuits and as reflectors for UWB antennas.

articleTitle: Influence of human body movement on mm wave communication in bullet train cars
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper examines the influence of the human body on the radio propagation characteristics of 60-GHz band mmWave (millimeter wave) communication systems in terms of the RSSI in the passenger car of bullet trains. We simulated the propagation characteristics of the 60-GHz band by a ray tracing method and investigated how many mmWave access points are necessary to meet the desired throughput at all the seats in the passenger car under the scenario that passengers enjoy the mmWave service while sitting in their seats. However, under scenarios such as a conductor or several passengers walking along the aisle from end to end through the passenger car, the propagation of mmWave is easily mitigated by obstructions such as the human body. So it is also important to further investigate to what extent human body movement along the aisle affects the RSSI of the STAs of those passengers sitting in their own seats. This paper first establishes a 3D simulation model of an ordinary passenger car and a 3D model of the human body. The simulation results numerically show the effect of human body movement and that the negative effect of human body movement can be absorbed if the mmWave APs are suitably allocated.

articleTitle: User-centric wireless access virtualization strategies for future 5G networks
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: User-centric wireless access virtualization (WAV) allows each user to be served by a set of carefully selected transmission points (TP)s forming a user-specific virtual basestation (uVBS) adapted to its environment and quality of service (QoS) requirement. In this way, this new concept breaks away from the conventional cell-centric architecture to provide boundaryless communications in future 5G networks. This fundamental structural 5G evolution alongside the ultra-dense multi-tier heterogenous context foreseen in such networks require an inevitable rethinking of efficient scalable TPs clustering. As such, this paper proposes three innovative low-cost clustering approaches that enable user-centric WAV and provide dynamic, adaptive, and overlapping TPs clusters while requiring not only negligible overhead and power costs, but also minimum signaling changes at both network and user sides. In contrast to existing clustering techniques, the new ones we propose better leverage 5G features such as extreme densification and massive connectivity as well as new concepts such as mmWave spectrum and massive MIMO. Furthermore, these approaches are flexible enough to be adapted to different network dimensions (i.e., space, time, etc.), thereby paving the way for achieving the dramatic performance improvements required by 5G networks to cope with the upcoming mobile data deluge.

articleTitle: Anonymous authentication based on cloud storage for cross-regional vehicles in VANET
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In VANET, remote network authentication servers can not authenticate the identity of vehicles without the aid of home domain authentication servers if the vehicles are in non-local regions, resulting in longer communication delay. To address this problem, an anonymous authentication scheme based on cloud storage (AABCS) for cross-regional vehicles in VANET is proposed. The secure cloud storage technology is used to build a public traffic cloud (TFC) as a storage media to avoid the problem of a single point failure. In the process of cross-regional authentication, vehicles first send the authentication request that contains the registration information to the non-local authentication server. Then, the non-local authentication server validates the vehicles directly through a round of information interaction. By security and performance analysis, the use of secure cloud storage technology can improve the efficiency of the cross-regional authentication in VANET without undermining the vehicle safety.

articleTitle: A compact bandpass filter with transmission zero based on SIW triangular cavities
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper proposes a compact bandpass cross - coupled substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filter with transmission zero. By using five triangular cavities as basic elements, a pentagon bandpass filter is designed and fabricated on a single-layer substrate with the standard printed circuit boards (PCB) process. This structure shows the advantages of compact SIW triangular cavity. Furthermore, by moving out some via-holes between input and output cavity, the cross-coupling is implemented conveniently, and a transmission zero at the upper sideband is realized.

articleTitle: Balanced-to-single-ended filtering power dividers
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Balanced-to-single-ended filtering power dividers have been used widely in modern communication systems due to their ability of easy connection with balanced and single-ended components simultaneously as well as differential-mode power division, common-mode suppression and filtering function, which is similar to balanced-to-balanced filtering power dividers. The conventional single-ended filtering power divider needs additional baluns to configure the balanced-to-balanced and balanced-to-single-ended filtering power divider, which results in large circuit size. Compared with balanced-to-balanced designs, few balanced-to-single-ended designs are reported. In this paper, two types of balanced-to-single-ended filtering power dividers are proposed and performances of them are compared.

articleTitle: A circular polarization reconfigurable substrate integrated waveguide antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, a cavity-backed substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) antenna with two reconfigurable circular polarizations is proposed and investigated. The circular polarizations are generated by a combination of complementary square split ring on the top layer and a shorting via between the top layer and the ground plane which introduces current perturbation. The polarization states of the proposed antenna can be dynamically switched between left-handed circular polarization (LHCP) and right-handed circular polarization (RHCP) by selectively connecting one of the two symmetrical shorting vias to the bottom ground plane. To validate our design, the proposed antenna is fabricated and measured. The simulated and experimental results are observed, which illustrates good performance of the proposed antenna. This single-port antenna polarization reconfigurable is useful for the design of array antenna for wireless applications.

articleTitle: Analysis and design of a 3.1–10.6 GHz wideband low-noise amplifier using resistive feedback
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A ultra-wideband(UWB) low noise amplifier(LNA) based on the cascade configuration is presented in this paper. Wideband input matching characteristic is obtained by making full use of the resistive shunt-shunt feedback combined with a parallel LC load to make the input network equivalent to a second-order wideband bandpass filter. In addition, the proposed LNA circuit is well fit for operating low supply voltage condition. Using a standard 0.18-um CMOS technology, the CMOS ultra-wideband LNA has been demonstrated for a frequency range of 3.1-10.6 GHz. Operated at a supply voltage of 0.8 V, the LNA dissipates 8.8-mW power and achieves a power gain of 13.8 ± 0.3dB, S11 below -10.5 dB, S22 below -14 dB, S12 below -25 dB, and noise figure(NF) ranging from 2.6 dB to 3.6 dB over the 3.1-10.6 GHz band of interest.

articleTitle: A 10-bit 100 MS/s CMOS current-steering DAC
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A 10-bit, 100MS/s digital-to-analog converter (DAC) is designed in a standard 0.18μm CMOS process, where a segmented current-steering technique is employed. Through elaborative comparison among different decoding strategies, a “6+4” segmented architecture is used to obtain a balance between area cost and performance. In order for excellent performance, an array of current sources based on a regulated cascode current mirror technique is used to achieve both high output impedance and large-swing output voltage. A latch with functions of amplitude limiting and clock synchronization is employed to reduce glitches and improve dynamic performance. From a single 1.8 V supply, simulation results show that a full-scale current of 8 mA, a differential non-linear (DNL) of ±0.1LSB, an integral nonlinear error (INL) of ±0.4LSB, and a spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) of 52dB are achieved.

articleTitle: Dual-band circularly polarized shared-aperture array with wideband and small frequency ratio
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A dual-band and dual-circularly polarized (CP) shared-aperture patch array antenna which can be fabricated on a single-layer substrate is proposed in this paper. The array is composed of two wideband CP subarrays operating at different frequencies. The CP senses of the two subarrays can be designed to be same or orthogonal according to the requirement. As one advantage, a small frequency ratio can be obtained easily. To achieve a wideband axial ratio (AR) performance and a compact structure, series-fed patches using sequence rotation technique are employed. An example is designed to show the effectiveness of the method. Simulation results show that bandwidths of 3.2% and 4.3% are obtained successfully for a dual-band dual-CP array operating at 6.83 GHz and 7.14 GHz, respectively, corresponding to a small frequency ratio of 1.05.

articleTitle: Miniaturized wide-stopband bandpass filter with high performance and easy design
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This article proposes a miniaturized wide-stopband bandpass filter on the combination of substrate integrated coaxial line (SICL) and in-resonator stub those possess superiority at wideband application and stopband extension respectively. Employing standard PCB process, high performance stopband with considerable suppression and extension is available, while corresponding design is fairly simple and straightforward.

articleTitle: A miniaturized tapered slot antenna with ultra-wide bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A miniaturized tapered slot antenna is proposed in this paper. The antipodal Vivaldi antenna is fed by the designed microstrip line and resistive loading is used to greatly reduce dimension of the antenna. In addition, a parasitic patch is stuck on the antenna to the increase the antenna's gain. The grid etched on the edge of the antenna is used to reduce the reflection and improve radiation performance. The dimension of the proposed antenna is 75mm × 74mm × 2mm. The measured results show that the bandwidth extends from 0.7 GHz to 6.2 GHz (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> <; -10dB), while the gain varies from -2dB to 9.4dB, which are in agreement with simulated results by HFSS. Due to the good radiation performance of the antenna, it can be used for ultra-wideband systems which have strict demand for dimension.

articleTitle: A novel compact dual-band branch-line coupler with cross-shaped stubs
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A cross-shaped branch-line coupler for dual-band applications is presented in this letter. The new structure uses a cross-shaped stub instead of one transmission line in the conventional branch-line coupler to work at two arbitrary frequencies. The two degrees of freedom have been introduced to have the flexible adjustment of the frequency ratio ranging from 2 to 7. The design equations are obtained by using ABCD-matrix. A new mathematical analysis has been used to discuss this structure. For verification, a dual-band branch-line coupler operating at 1 and 3.5 GHz has been designed and measured on a Rogers' RO4003 board which has a compact size of 0.022λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A novel coupling mode based 3D MIMO channel modeling and capacity analysis for 5G
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Three-dimension (3D) MIMO is considered as one of the key technologies for the fifth generation (5G) communication systems. In order to better assess the system performance, it is essential to build a corresponding accurate 3D channel model. This paper proposes a 3D Weichselberger model by structuring a novel coupling matrix, which is derived from 3D WINNER channel model. Specifically, the 3D Weichselberger model is developed for arbitrary antenna arrays and arbitrary propagation environment. In addition, our proposed coupling matrix not only reduces the complexity, but also considers the joint-dependence between transmitter and receiver for 3D Weichselberger model. Moreover, the channel capacity of 3D Weichselberger model is analyzed. Simulation results are provided to confirm the proposed model.

articleTitle: Investigations on anti-jamming method for 77GHz automotive millimeter-wave radar
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: LSFCW modulation system, presented by this paper based on LFMCW, is more suitable for 77GHz millimeter-wave radar system to identify the target, which takes advantages of the modulation of FSK and LFMCW; and implements multiple target real-time detection ability whether stationary or movement. By means of the chip of ADF4159 from ANALOG DEVICES supporting the modulation of FSK and LFMCW, the fast sawtooth sweep frequency is implemented from 12.765GHz to 12.815GHz; the function of the automotive millimeter-wave radar frequency hopping is realized by means of the frequency of FSK set by properly.

articleTitle: Energy efficiency in multi-source network-coded device-to-device cooperative communications
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Many researchers have recently proposed adopting relays to enhance performance in device-to-device (D2D) communication systems. With D2D technology, geographically closed terminals can be connected directly. By this means, information delivery in many practical application scenarios (e.g., in a shopping mall, a number of shops intend to distribute their vouchers/advertisements to potential customers in the vicinity) can be conducted more efficiently. In this paper we consider a wireless multi-source multi-destination D2D content distribution network and propose a network-coding based cooperative transmission scheme. Through system achievable energy efficiency analysis, we exhibit the potential benefits of applying network coding and user cooperation in future D2D communication systems.

articleTitle: Planar slot antenna based on triangle substrate integrated waveguide cavity
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A novel, low-profile cavity backed slot antenna is proposed. The antenna consists of a thin equilateral triangle substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity with a single radiating slot at upper edge which is fed by a grounded co-planar waveguide (GCPW) to excite the TE110 mode. Measurement results indicate that the antenna achieves a good gain of 6.36 dBi and low cross polarization level, which shows that this antenna retains good radiation performance of conventional cavity backed antennas. Besides, the planar antenna possesses the attractive characteristics including light weight, low-profile, simple structure, easy to be fabricated with low cost and convenient integration with planar circuit.

articleTitle: Low-cost phase shifter and calibration solution for multi-channel receiver
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: The design of a multi-channel receiver phase shifter based vector multiplier for high performance and low-cost active antenna array is presented in this paper. A receiving array architecture that combines analog beamforming is to offer a solution for the phase array and smart antenna application. In the architecture, a system with simple calibration procedure is presented to decrease the phase deviation with phase shift and gain control. Therefore, continuously adjustable 360° phase with resolution 0.18° control can be achieved.

articleTitle: An efficient 2-D DOA estimation algorithm for coherent signals
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: For two-dimensional(2-D) direction-of-arrival(DOA) estimation of coherent signals, this paper proposes a new algorithm based on matrix reconstruction and polynomial rooting. Extracting the first column of the correlation matrix and constructing a new matrix by utilizing the conjugate symmetry property. The column rank of the new matrix is exactly equal to number of sources and has no relationship with sources' relevance. Constructing the polynomial with the new orthogonal matrix and then solving it to get the estimation. The new algorithm has low computational complexity and has higher performance than spatial smoothing, Toeplitz reconstruction algorithms, etc. Simulations demonstrate the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of a dual-polarized patch array for millimeter-wave applications
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-polarized patch array is designed, fabricated, and measured at millimeter-wave band. This antenna array consists of two layers of substrates, and stacked square patches are adopted. The measured impedance bandwidth for the two ports is <;-10dB from 27 GHz to 29 GHz, and the measured isolation between the two ports is better than 36 dB within the bandwidth. The measured gains of the two ports at 28 GHz are 19.7 dBi and 19.1 dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: Simulation and design on receiver front-end at S band
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, a high gain receiver front-end is proposed. The full-wave analysis method is used to simulate the PCB with box. Combined with electromagnetic field simulation, the front-end circuit electrical specifications are analyzed by ADS. According to the simulation, the receiver front-end is fabricated and tested. The test results are agreed with the simulation. The working bandwidth is about 22MHz. the frontend test gain is more than 80dB, and system noise figure is about 3dB.

articleTitle: Design of a low-profile dual circularly polarized phased array antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A low-profile dual circularly polarized antenna array is proposed, employing cavity-backed patch antenna as elements. Circular polarization is obtained by feeding a pair of orthogonal linear polarization simultaneously with 90° phase shift using a branch-line coupler. The antenna element achieves impedance bandwidth of 32.8% (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>|<;-10dB) and isolation bandwidth of 17.1% (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</sub>|<;-10dB). The sequentially rotated 2×2 subarray exhibits impedance bandwidth of 15% (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>|<;-10dB) and the axial ratio remains below 0.08dB. The overall height of the antenna is 12.5mm, which is about 0.1λ at the center frequency 2.4GHz. Simulation results show that the 2×8 array achieves a wide beam scanning capability of ±60°.

articleTitle: Body obstruction characteristics for off-body channel under hospital environment at 6∼8.5 GHz
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: The statistical characteristics of body obstruction (BO) and none-BO (NBO) cases for off-body channel under hospital environment at 6∼8.5 GHz are presented in this paper. It is seen that all the statistical parameters of off-body channel in BO and NBO cases share the same distributions except the RMS. It is also found that the relationship between RMS and coherence bandwidth under BO and NBO cases fits both the inverse proportion relationship and exponential function well. By comparing the aforementioned distributions and the relationship parameters between RMS and coherence bandwidth, the off-body channel in BO case generates more complex multi-path components and signal degradation than the NBO one. The presented results of body obstruction characteristics could be used to develop the physical layer and improve the performance for off-body channel communication.

articleTitle: A novel magneto-electric dipole antenna with a differential feeding structure
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A novel magneto-electric dipole antenna with a differential feeding structure is proposed in this paper. The antenna is composed of a horizontal circular electric dipole, two semicircular shorted patches as a magneto dipole, and a rectangular cavity. A differential feeding structure is employed as a perfect balun to feed the antenna. The simulated results show that the antenna achieves impedance bandwidth of 89% from 4.0GHz to 10.4GHz, with VSWR≤2. A high and stable gain of 10.45 ± 1.45dBi is obtained over the operating frequency range via a rectangular cavity. In addition, the symmetrical radiation patterns of E- and H-plane with high front-to-back ratio (≥16dB) and low cross polarization (≤-40dB) are realized.

articleTitle: An ultra-wideband variable gain low noise amplifier
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-wideband variable gain low noise amplifier (UWB-VGLNA). At the input stage, a common-emitter and common-base amplifier with serial-parallel feedback network and active bias network was used to achieve good wideband input impedance matching. At gain-tuning stage, a combinational circuit consisting of active inductor load and Darlington cascode amplifier with gain tuning transistor was employed to not only realize the tunable output gain, but also increase gain and achieve greater gain tunable range. At the output stage, a common-collector amplifier with tunable current mirror was designed to achieve good wideband output impedance matching and extend gain-tuning range. The UWB-VGLNA is designed based on the standard WIN 0.2μm GaAs HBT process. The UWB-VGLNA showed S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> tunable range from 8.7dB to 29.1dB; the S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> of less than -10dB; the S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</sub> of less than -11dB; the NF of less than 4.3dB; the stability coefficient (Mu1) of over 3. The static power consumption is less than 34mW under the operation voltage of 4 V.

articleTitle: Low-profile circularly polarized Fabry-Perot antenna fed by air-coupling microstrip patch
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A circularly polarized Fabry-Perot resonator (FPR) antenna is presented in this paper, which is feed by air-coupled patch antenna. The circular polarization wave is excited by an equilateral triangle patch and cross-shaped gap on the metal ground plane. The FPR resonator consists of a partially reflective surface (PRS) formed by rhombus slot frequency selective surface (FSS) and metal ground plane. The profile of the prototype has reduced to nearly a quarter of a wavelength. The measured results and simulated results are approximately accordant and a peak gain of 18.7 dB can be achieved, which is higher than that of common single-feed patch antennas and the proposed antenna has a common frequency bandwidth of 3.5% for S11 ≤ -10dB, gain-drop ≤ 3dB, and axial ratio ≤ 3dB.

articleTitle: TCP enhancement technology in cognitive network based on cross-layer designing
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: The difference between cognitive wireless network and traditional wireless network lies in the function of spectrum sensing and channel switching. In cognitive networks, cognitive users must sense the spectrum. When the primary users access, it must switch to another channel in order to avoid the interference to the primary users. Therefore, it is necessary to improve the traditional TCP to make it adapt to the spectrum sensing and channel switching in cognitive network. The cross-layer designing between TCP and MAC can eliminate retransmission problems caused by the spectrum sensing, and the proposed “TCP-improved algorithm” can solve the problems of low utilization rate of bandwidth or network congestion when cognitive users switch its channel. The experimental results show that the “TCP-improved algorithm” has the best performance in cognitive network.

articleTitle: Wide-locking range divide-by-5 injection-locked frequency divider using linear mixer approach for microwave device application
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A novel divide-by-5 injection-locked frequency divider (ILFD) is proposed and was implemented in the TSMC 0.18 pm 1P6M CMOS process. Conventional harmonic mixer divide-by-5 ILFD has limited locking range, this letter shows a wide locking range divide-by-5 ILFD designed with linear mixer technique. At the drain-source bias of 1.2 V and at the incident power of 0 dBm, the locking range of the divide-by-5 is 2 GHz, from the incident frequency 13.1 GHz to 15.1 GHz, the percentage is 14.18%. The core power consumption under the injection-locked condition is 4.2mW. The free-running oscillation frequency is 2.73GHz. The die area is 0.861 × 0.848 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The proposed ILFD is based on a cross-coupled voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO).

articleTitle: An integration of dual-band filtering antenna for WLAN application
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A compact dual-band filtering antenna is proposed for WLAN(2.4G/5.2G) Application. It is a integrated design of a step impedance resonators dual-band bandpass filter and a patch antenna using aperture coupled feed techniques. The patch antenna can be viewed as a radiator but also the last resonator of the dual-band bandpass filter. Compared with traditional wireless communication system, the filtering antenna leaves out the 50 Ω transmission line instead of an aperture coupled structure, thus, no more additional space is needed, which makes the size more compact. Besides, the proposed filtering antenna provides a high band-edge gain selectivity.

articleTitle: Wide band compact RF receiver for millimeter wave 5G mobile communication
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A wide band compact RF receiver front-end for 5G communication system is designed in this paper, which could be typically applied in a Q-band millimeter wave massive MIMO system of 16 channels. The RF receiver is designed using multi-layered structure and highly-integrated downconverter chips to decrease the module size. The antenna feeding transition structure is designed using electromagnetic field simulation software, and integrated in RF board. The size of fabricated RF receiver is 2cm∗2cm. IF and power supply circuits are also designed separately to support the RF array with 16 channels configuration. The performance of single channel receiver in the array is measured with gain of 26.9dB, gain flatness of 1.13dB, input 1dB compression point of −6dBm, third-order intercept point of 5.3dBm and the EVM of 1.6%rms.

articleTitle: Crowd-based personal radars for indoor mapping using UWB measurements
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: The concept of personal radar has recently emerged as an interesting solution for future simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) applications. In this paper we evaluate the performance of an ultrawide-band (UWB) radar system for indoor environments mapping by exploiting a grid-based Bayesian approach able to combine all the measurements collected by radars adopting non-pencil beam antennas. In the proposed approach, the crowd will be involved by freely exploring the space, sending environmental partial views of it to cloud servers, where a complete map will be formed. Results show how the mapping accuracy can be improved thanks to the information collected from the crowd and considering different receivers schemes.

articleTitle: A novel design of broadband Quasi-Yagi antenna loaded with split-ring resonators
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A novel broadband Quasi-Yagi antenna is presented. The antenna is feed by a microstrip line. A new balun structure is used to realized transform from microstrip line to coplanar strip line. It has a radiator and two directors, the ground plane at the bottom of the substrate act as reflector. The bandwidth is relatively broad. To enhance the gain, two group of split-ring resonators (SRR) is loaded on the front of the directors. The -10dB return loss bandwidth of the improved antenna reached 53.7%(5.9-10.2Ghz), 5.7~9.3dB gain is attained, about 2dB more than the prototype antenna. Both the prototype antenna and the improved antenna are fabricated and measured. The measured results agree with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: A 1–6GHz ultra broadband multiple-channel integrated receiver
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper presents a 1–6GHz ultra broadband multiple-channel integrated receiver. The total dimension of the receiver with 7 channels is 200×220×26mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The noise figure of the receiver is less than 2.5dB, the harmonics suppression is greater than 47dBc, the amplitude consistency of the channels is better than 1dB, and the phase consistency of the channels is less than ±5°.

articleTitle: A 34.5GHz planar magic-T based on coupling slot and substrate integrated waveguide
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, a ka-band magic-T using substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) and coupling slot is proposed and developed for microwave applications on the basis of the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. Due to the metal ground between the input and output ports the planar magic-T consists of a 180 degree phase-reversal junction and an H-plane SIW T-junction. Theoretical analyses and the optimized wideband magic-T structure is demonstrated and discussed with the models of the magic-T. The magic-T is simulated with a 3D FEM electromagnetic simulation software and the results are presented. The frequency bandwidth is 20.3%, when the simulated VSWR of the port of the magic-T is less than 1.5 from 31GHz to 38GHz, and the simulated amplitude imbalance is less than ±0.22dB, and the simulated phase imbalance is less than ±0.8°, and the simulated isolation between the sum port and the difference port is higher than 43dB.

articleTitle: Design of a low phase noise LO module for IEEE 802.11ac system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: The design of a low-phase-noise local oscillator (LO) module for RF transceivers which support the very high throughput mode of IEEE 802.11ac standard is presented in this paper. This LO module provides both intermediate frequency (IF) LO and radio frequency (RF) LO by using HMC83x series chips. Low pass filters and amplifiers are used to improve output power and suppress harmonics of LO signals. Experimental results show that the designed LO module can generate IF LO signal at 1.05GHz and RF LO signal at a range from 4GHz to 5GHz with 20MHz step. The measured in-band phase noise is -116.14dBc/Hz for 1.05GHz carriers and out-of-band phase noise is -142.51dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset. As to RF LO, the measured in-band phase noise is below 107.48dBc/Hz at 10 KHz offset and out-of-band phase noise is below -132dBc/Hz in a range from 4GHz to 5GHz.

articleTitle: A dualband and broadband antenna array for ambient RF energy harvesting
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, a new 2×2 circular microstrip antenna array with air dielectric layer for ambient RF energy harvesting has been proposed. Two pairs of arc-shaped slots located close to the boundary of the circular microstrip patch has been designed for making dualband and extending the frequency bandwidth. The antenna has the frequency bandwidth from 1.85GHz to 1.93GHz and from 2.0GHz to 2.1GHz which can cover GSM-1800 and UMTS-2100 bands. At the frequency of 1.89GHz and 2.05GHz, the measured gain is 5.3dBi and 6.6dBi, respectively, and high gain of 3.8dBi–9.3dBi has been achieved over the whole band.

articleTitle: A dual-band stacked-patch satellite antenna with parasitic elements for axial ratio beamwidth enhancement
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A novel stacked-patch circularly polarized (CP) antenna with enhanced axial ratio (AR) performance is investigated and designed for s-band satellite communication applications. Through structure modification and parameter study, the optimized antenna dimensions are obtained. The antenna exhibits an AR beamwidth enhancement of about 38.6% at dual-band with the parasitic elements addition compared to the original design. The performances of the proposed antenna are verified in detail in terms of the reflection coefficients, axial ratio, and the radiation pattern in simulation in the end.

articleTitle: Realising energy-aware communication over fading channels under QoS constraints
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: There exists a trade-off between energy consumption and spectral efficiency in wireless communication systems under quality of service (QoS) constraints. This paper studies the use of effective capacity theory to characterise the maximum supported channel capacity over fading channels whilst considering both QoS constraints and energy consumption. Moreover, a generalised fading channel model, i.e., the hyper Fox's H fading model, is considered that includes many practical fading channel models as special cases, e.g., Rayleigh, Rician, Weibull and Nakagami-m fading channel models. The results are readily applicable to design energy-aware communication systems over fading channels with QoS constraints, e.g., wireless sensor networks and smart grid communication systems.

articleTitle: Principle of vector synthesis predistortion linearizers controlling AM/AM and AM/PM independently
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper using vector diagram illuminates the operation principle of vector synthesis predistortions and proves they can control amplitude modulation to amplitude modulation (AM/AM) and amplitude modulation to phase modulation (AM/PM) separately. A vector synthesis predistortion linearizer is designed to verify this thought and the results show the correctness of this thought.

articleTitle: Design of a bandpass differentiator based on network synthesis methods
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A bandpass differentiator based on network synthesis methods is designed in this paper. The synthesis methods can implement arbitrary response with frequency. If the transfer function S21 is specified, the stability of the differentiator can be ensured absolutely by chosen the left half-plane roots of F(s). The K/J inverter is designed to implement the coupled circuit. Then, a microwave differentiator is designed and simulated. The simulated results of the differentiator show good agreement with the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: A shared-aperture dual circularly polarized antenna array for satellite communication
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A dual circularly polarized antenna array with high gain, good axial ratio and low sidelobes for satellite communication is proposed. The shared-aperture antenna can realize right-hand circularly polarized (RHCP) and left-hand circularly polarized (LHCP) radiation simultaneously at S band by using a directional coupler connected with an H-shaped aperture coupling network and a coplanar microstrip feed network. The two feed networks, which share the same ground in the center, are arranged on the both sides of the ground respectively. This arrangement ensures a good linearly polarization purity and thus good RHCP and LHCP characteristics. In order to reduce the sidelobes of the antenna array, the whole array is divided into sixteen sub arrays of 2×2 elements. The amplitudes of the 16 sub-array are arranged appropriately in a taper distribution which can be realized by a relatively simple feeding network. The simulation results show that the as-designed 8×8 antenna array has a very good performance: a -10dB return loss bandwidth of 20%, a -3dB axial ratio bandwidth of 18%, a 35dB copolar-crosspolar ratio level and the peak gains better than 25dBi for both RHCP and LHCP radiation with sidelobes below -18dB.

articleTitle: Capacitive loading comb-shaped tri-polarized MIMO slot antennas
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Design of three orthogonal polarized slot antennas with capacitive loading is presented. The elements are identical slot antennas with slits on both sides of the slot. The radiating slot is loaded with capacitor that becomes step impedance resonator (SIR) structure to miniaturize the antennas. The size of the antennas can be reduced to 61.4%. Simulations and measurements show they work at 2.45GHz with a 150MHz bandwidth. The radiation characteristics of the size-reduced antennas are almost similar to the unloaded slot, with the low cross-polarization levels. The antennas can be used in multi-polarized MIMO system.

articleTitle: A compact quasi-millimeter-wave microstrip wideband bandpass filter
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, a quasi-millimeter-wave wideband bandpass filter (BPF) is designed by using a microstrip dual-mode ring resonator and two folded half-wavelength resonators. Based on the transmission line equivalent circuit of the filter, variations of the frequency response of the filter versus the circuit parameters are investigated first by using the derived formulas and circuit simulators. Then a BPF with a 3dB fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 20% at 25.5 GHz is designed, which realizes the desired wide passband, sharp skirt property, and very wide stopband. Finally, the designed BPF is fabricated, and its measured frequency response is found agree well with the simulated result.

articleTitle: A compact planar magic-T using quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide resonator and slotline coupling transition
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A compact planar magic-T based on the quarter mode substrate integrated waveguide (QMSIW) resonator is proposed in this paper. A slot line is etched in the bottom layer to couple the energy out of the power divider and functions as the H arm of the Magic-T. The planar magic-T has a wideband characteristic since the QMSIW resonator has a very low Q factor, which has been demonstrated by the simulation results. The agreement between the simulation results and the measured data has verified the design of this wideband magic-T.

articleTitle: Preliminary studies on the coupled antennas and feedlines using natural boundary conditions
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, the coupling mechanism between antennas and feedlines are conceptually studied by analyzing the respective natural boundary condition of the antenna and the feedline. Different cases of the coupling between typical antennas and feedlines are discussed, analyzed and compared. When the natural boundary conditions of the antennas and the feedlines are less matched, the coupled antenna-feedline systems tend to exhibit more notable unbalanced effects. Preliminary simulated and experimental results are presented to validate the theoretic results. Finally, two remarks are drawn and expected to provide possible design guidelines in future novel antenna developments.

articleTitle: I/Q imbalance calibration in wideband direct-conversion receivers
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A wideband correction technique is proposed to calibrate the I/Q imbalance of wideband direct-conversion receivers (DCR). The wide bandwidth of input signal is divided into a series of narrow-band in which the I/Q mismatches are frequency-dependent. By using test signals in above narrow-band, the correction coefficients a and b can be calculated at corresponding frequencies. And then the coefficient curves over the whole wideband can be obtained based on cubic spline interpolation. With this method, the image rejection ratio (IRR) of DCR is generally increased 30dBc in the whole band after calibration, and the performance is improved significantly.

articleTitle: Gain enhancement for microstrip antenna with zero-index metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A wideband microstrip antenna fed by a modified T-shaped probe is presented for 60-GHz applications. In order to improve the gain performance, a novel Zero-Index Metamaterial (ZIM) is loaded at the top of the proposed antenna. The zero permittivity point of the proposed ZIM structure is acquired at the frequency around 60-GHz. Two antennas are simulated for a comparison, the antenna loaded with ZIM cells and the one without ZIM cells. The antenna loaded with ZIM cells exhibits a gain enhancement of up to 3.1dB in the frequency band of 55–70 GHz. The impedance bandwidth for SWR≤2 is about 30% from the frequency band of 55–70 GHz.

articleTitle: Evaluating a QoS aware path selection service using the GENI network
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Smart homes, cars, offices and schools can significantly improve the quality of our life. The traditional networks are not sufficient to provide the service needed for these future smart management systems due to their lack of flexibility. This paper proposes an application-aware service that can select and set an alternative forwarding path based on the measurement of the Quality of Service of paths in the software defined networks. The proposed service is evaluated by developing experiments using the GENI network. The results demonstrate that our service can make routing decisions based on the application requirement and measurement about the current state of the network, and greatly improve the routing performance over the default method used in existing networks.

articleTitle: Novel low-power ternary explicit pulsed JKL flip-flop based on CNFET
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A novel single-edge explicit pulsed JKL flip-flop (S-JKL) and dual-edge explicit pulsed JKL flip-flop (D-JKL) are designed with Carbon Nanotube Field Effect Transistor (CNFET). Firstly, a single-edge pulsed generator (S-PG) is designed. Then combined with a ternary JKL latch, a S-JKL is obtained; D-JKL is designed by replacing S-PG with double-edge pulsed generator (D-PG). The circuits possess the character of high speed and low power by employing CNFET. The scheme is simulated by HSPICE, and the results show that the designed ternary explicit pulsed JKL flip-flop has correct logic function and low power consumption.

articleTitle: JS-RAKE: Judiciously trained selective RAKE receiver for UWB systems
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Hardware complexity reduction is critically important for Rake receivers in ultra-wide band systems, where the number of channel multi-path components (MPCs) can be very large. Though several designs (S-Rake, P-Rake) have been proposed, the impact of channel estimation overhead has not been accounted for in prior literature. In this paper, we propose a new Judiciously trained Selective Rake receiver that performs channel estimation for only a subset of the many channel multi-path components. The intuition behind the design is that only a few channel MPCs have enough strength to make them sufficiently likely to contribute significantly to the received signal power. By restricting the channel estimation to only these MPCs, the estimation overhead can be reduced significantly without degrading capacity. In this paper, we first show that if the MPCs have independent Rayleigh amplitude fading, it is data rate optimal to perform channel estimation for only a subset of the MPCs with the highest second-order moments. We also present a closed form expression for the achievable data-rate of a JS-Rake receiver in Rayleigh fading and find the data-rate maximizing size of this subset. Simulations in several practically relevant channel settings show that JS-Rake boosts data rate by 30-40% and 50%, in comparison to S-Rake and P-Rake, respectively.

articleTitle: Ultra-broadband and low phase noise frequency synthesizer
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper proposes a high performance frequency synthesizer system featured by ultra-broadband, low phase noise. In order to achieve frequency synthesizer covering 0.4~18GHz with 10MHz step, two PLL (Phase Locked Loop), mixer, microwave switch, multiplier, frequency divider, and band-pass filter are been used. The three-section frequency VCO is use to generate 4.5~9GHz frequency signal. The 0.4~0.45GHz frequency signal is obtained by division of 4.5~9GHz frequency signal, and the 9~18GHz signal is obtained by frequency doubler of 4.5~9GHz frequency signal. The frequency synthesizer's output power level is -50dBm~0dBm, the phase noise is better than -85dBc/Hz@1KHz, and the suppression to spurious is better than -55dBc.

articleTitle: A compact bandpass SIW filter with transmission zero at lower frequency side
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, a compact bandpass filter with substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) triangular cavities is proposed. Using negative coupling technology, a bandpass filter with transmission zero has been designed and fabricated on a single-layer substrate. Adopting three little triangular cavities as basic elements, the resonator filter can be fabricated by the standard printed circuit boards (PCB) process. This structure gives full expression to the advantages of cross-coupling and compact SIW triangular cavity. Not only the compact structure, but also the inverse feedback is the characteristic of the bandpass filter. The cross-coupled technique makes a sharper transition performance at the lower sideband and a great promotion to outband.

articleTitle: A miniature RFID tag antenna mounted on metallic objects
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper proposed a miniature UHF-RFID tag antenna designed for metallic objects. The antenna structure consists of a T-matching network, double symmetrical radiating patches on top and a ground plane at bottom. The miniature design is achieved by adding capacitive tip loadings at the end of the two radiating patches respectively to increase the capacitive reactance of the antenna, so the self-resonant tends to 915MHZ. The bandwidth (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| less than -10dB) is about 80MHz and it covers two main frequency bands.

articleTitle: A short revisit of nonlinear Gaussian filters: State-of-the-art and some concerns
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Since the landmark work of the Kalman filter in the 1960s, considerable effort has been devoted to a variety of novel filters for nonlinear estimation. Among them, the class of nonlinear Gaussian filters plays a key role. This paper briefly revisits the state-of-the-art developments, highlights a part of interesting and new findings and raises some of our concerns.

articleTitle: Design and testing for phase stabilized based on optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
