Performance of the antenna, such as S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>, radiation patterns and gain, are simulated and compared with the original quasi-Yagi antenna. As is presented in this paper, the impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna is from 7.98GHz to 13.84GHz, about 53%. Good directivity, low cross polarization level(lower than -20dB) and high gain(over 8.88dB at the center frequency) are achieved by optimizing the structure. Due to the simplified feed network and easy fabrication, the proposed antenna will have wide appilications in telecommunication.

articleTitle: Q-band linear power amplifier for backhaul application
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper presents a Q-band linear power amplifier (PA) designed for wideband high order M-QAM transmission scenario aiming for backhaul application. The linear PA consists of multiple stage amplifier with variable gain, complemented with digital predistortion (DPD). Variable gain characteristic of the proposed PA is analyzed based on the application scenario and implemented upconverter architecture. The proposed amplifier utilizes dynamic bias control to adjust its gain and digital predistortion is adopted to enhance the linearity of PA. Experimental measurement of digital predistortion on Q-band PA is conducted and the proposed implement achieves average output power of 16dBm, ACPR of-50dBc whereas current drop from 900mA to 400mA.

articleTitle: A new efficient flexible GMRES for solving surface integral equation of PMCHWT
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper presents a new flexible GMRES for solving surface integral equation (SIE). In the proposed method, JMCFIE is set as the inner iteration to accelerate the convergence speed, while PMCHWT is set as the outer iteration to guarantee the accuracy. In addition, multilevel fast mutilpole algorithm (MLFMA) is used to reduce the memory of impedance matrix and improve the computational efficiency. The method is validated by comparisons with the analytic Mie solution and the conventional flexible GMRES, to illustrate the accuracy and high efficiency, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of a wideband bandpass filter with dual-mode resonators
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband bandpass filter (BPF) with dual-mode resonators (DMRs) is proposed and designed by a novel approach. The DMR is equivalent to separate a λ stepped-impedance resonator (SIR) and λ/2 uniform impedance resonator (UIR). The design procedure is step-by-step so as to analysis the circuit structure clearly. Then the dimensions of DMRs can be determined analytically. Moreover, the proposed wideband BPF has the merits of low insertion losses, good return losses and wide stopband. The simulated and measured results are in good agreement.

articleTitle: A microwave gain equalizer based on non-degenerate mode resonators
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A gain equalizer is designed based on non-degenerate dual-mode sector cavities. Two orthogonal coupling slots are implemented to excite two non-degenerate modes in the cavity. One of the dual-mode frequencies can be tuned by perturbation via. And the positions of the film resistors loaded on the resonator are investigated to realize attenuations and Q-factor of the non-degenerate tuning independent. Compared with equalizers based on single-mode resonators, the proposed equalizer cuts in half the number of resonators, and it keeps the original performance, so it has more compact volume. The measured results are in good agreement with the simulated results.

articleTitle: Design of a UHF RFID receiver based on 0.18-μm CMOS technology
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Radio frequency identification (RFID) technology has been widely applied in many fields such as anti-counterfeiting, access control system and security management system. The main modules of the receiver are designed and simulationed basised on SMIC 0.18-μm CMOS technology. The low noise amplifier (LNA) consists of two stages of circuits. The first stage is a source inductance feedback amplifier and the second stage is a cascode structure amplifier, which makes the gain and noise figure improved effectively. An improved Gilibert active dual balanced mixer is used to improve the noise and conversion gain by using the static current injection and the local oscillator buffer technique, and the output buffer is added to enhance the mixer conversion gain and linearity. Finally, a zero IF receiver is implemented by the designed LNA and two I/Q branches of mixers. The simulation results show that the receiver gives 19.14 dB gain with 8.31dB noise figure, and the input 1dB compression point of 2.37dBm. It meets the requirement of RF front-end in 900MHz-RFID receiver.

articleTitle: Simulation and analysis of multipath propagation characteristics for UWB in the indoor radio channels based on SBR/IM
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, the propagation characteristics of UWB (Ultra-wideband) signal in the indoor radio channels are discussed based on the method of SBR/IM (Shooting and bouncing ray tracing/image). Propagation characteristics are analyzed by considering of multipath propagation mechanisms including direct ray, reflection and transmission. A good agreement is achieved between the measured results and simulated results, so the correctness of the SBR/IM method has been validated. Some channel propagation characteristic parameters of UWB are discussed in the simulated results, such as values of the path loss, the distribution of the received power, the time-domain electric field intensity. Also, path loss exponent is deduced from the simulated results. The analysis of the above results may be provide the theoretical basis for wireless communication network coverage and optimization of UWB signal in the complex environment of indoor.

articleTitle: Simulation of 38 GHz millimeter-wave propagation characteristics in the indoor environment
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, the propagation characteristics of 38GHz millimeter wave in an indoor environment are simulated based on ray tracing method. The path loss and delay spread are discussed and analyzed on both line of sight and non line of sight. The conclusions drawn in this thesis may be utilized for the design of millimeter-wave mobile communications for the future fifth generation cellular system.

articleTitle: A novel LDPC decoder based on coarse-grained reconfigurable array
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel LDPC decoder based on Coarse-Grained Reconfigurable Array, named RaSP-D (Reconfigurable Signal Processor for Decoder). According to the Normalized Min-Sum (NMS) Algorithm, the fusion-step routing structure with corresponding mapping strategy is implemented in the proposed RaSP-D. The verification of RaSP-D is based on TSMC 45nm craft, and the processor works at the frequency of 300MHz. The experimental results show that the average array utilization rate of RaSP-D with proposed mapping strategy can be up to 80% in regular LDPC codes. The peak throughput of RaSP-D is over 1 Gbps, which satisfies the LTE-A standard. Besides, the RaSP-D supports 4 kinds of code rates with the code range of 576~2304 bit. Compared with the state-of-the-art architectures, such as ASICs, DSPs and CGRAs, RaSP-D achieves larger range of code rate, higher throughput and higher flexibility with dynamic reconfiguration.

articleTitle: High-efficiency Huygens' surfaces for electromagnetic wave controlling
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A Huygens' surface that efficiently refracts normally incident electromagnetic waves at 12 GHz is reported. The phase gradient along the interface is modulated by four isotropic, non-resonant, spatial phase shifters with dimensions of 0.5λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.5λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the free-space wavelength at 12 GHz. The electric and magnetic responses of the unit cells are controlled by metallic patterns etched on multilayer dielectric substrates. Then, these surface structures are used to fabricate a high-efficiency microwave lens with F/D to be 0.27. The simulation results show that the peak value of the transmission efficiency approaches 97.6%.

articleTitle: Improved algorithms for high-dimensional robust PCA
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Principal component analysis (PCA) is one of the most crucial dimensionality reduction methods and widely used in satellite image analysis, face recognition, social network feature extraction and other application scenarios. But it is fragile because of its quadratic error criterion when faced with outliers. There are many robust PCAs to solve this problem, however, when extended to the high-dimensional set, in which the dimensionality of dataset is comparable to the number of observations, the quality of their output will suffer dramatically. So the high-dimensional robust PCA is needed eagerly. HR-PCA and DHR-PCA are exactly the algorithms designed for this regime. They are robust and fit for high-dimensional space. However, attention has to be paid to the low efficiency and loss of useful information respectively in these two algorithms. Two improved algorithms are proposed in this paper to address these issues. Firstly, a preprocessing mechanism is added before performing HR-PCA so as to reduce the burden of HR-PCA. Secondly, we take different ways of changing weights of observations according to their outlyingness instead of decreasing all weights in DHR-PCA. From the simulation results, the improved algorithms are robust enough and have stable performance.

articleTitle: An architecture for frequency hopping cognitive radio networks
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: The radio frequency (RF) spectrum is a limited resource. Spectrum allotment disputes stem from this scarcity as many radio devices are confined to a fixed frequency or frequency sequence. One alternative is to incorporate cognition within a reconfigurable radio platform, therefore enabling the radio to adapt to dynamic RF spectrum environments. In this way, the radio is able to actively observe the RF spectrum, orient itself to the current RF environment, decide on a mode of operation, and act accordingly, thereby sharing the spectrum and operating in more flexible manner. This research presents a novel framework for incorporating several techniques for the purpose of adapting radio operation to the current RF environment.

articleTitle: Novel spectrum sharing model and leasing strategy for multiple operators
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Traditional static spectrum allocation can not adapt to the future development of wireless communication services, leading to limited profits for operators and poor Quality of Service (QoS) for users. Aiming at the problem, this paper proposes a three-layer spectrum sharing model in which A operators place their excess spectrum in the leasing platform for B operators to lease. The situation in which multiple operators cooperate to share portions of spectrum but compete to serve users is considered in this paper, then the optimal spectrum leasing strategy is studied. The goal of this paper is to find the optimal leasing strategy for both A and B operators to maximize their profits while guaranteeing the QoS for users. Numerical results show that the proposed strategy not only improves the efficiency of spectrum utilization effectively but also shows a big advantage in increasing operators' profits.

articleTitle: A new ultra-wide band characteristic basis function method based on interpolation scheme
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, a new ultra-wide band characteristic basis function method based on interpolation scheme(IN-UCBFM)has been proposed for analyzing the wide band electromagnetic scattering problems. By virtual of matrix interpolation for impedance matrices and wide-band characteristic basis functions based on interpolation scheme, the IN-UCBFM not only can greatly reduce the number of unknowns, but also can globally shorten the calculation time. The numerical example and comparisons suggest the accuracy and the efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of a novel wideband multi-frequency patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A kind of isosceles right triangle patch antenna which works in 2.9GHz frequency is designed based on the cavity model theory. A wideband multi-frequency patch antenna is designed and fabricated using the metameterial via the periodically loaded complementary split-ring resonators on the upper patch and strip-line gaps on the bottom ground plane, respectively, besides, intercepting a part of bottom ground plane below the patch to enhance the gain at higher frequency part. The simulation results show that the patch antenna presents the desired four bandwidths which cover all the 2.4/5.2/5.8GHz Bluetooth/RFID/WLAN bands and the 2.5/3.5GHz WiMAX band, including 0.29GHz(2.33GHz ~2.62GHz), 1.01 GHz(3.11 GHz~4.12GHz), 0.39GHz(4.97~5.36GHz), 0.41 GHz(5.74~6.15GHz). Due to the fact that the effective medium parameters of substrate of antenna are affected by the left-hand characteristic, the wave propagation direction of antenna is changed, which induces the strongest radiation in horizontal direction rather than the vertical direction of the conventional patch antenna at higher frequency part.

articleTitle: A low power variable gain wideband low noise amplifier
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A low power variable gain wideband low noise amplifier (LPVG-LNA) was designed in this paper by using active inductor and multiple current reuse circuit structures. At the input stage of LPVG-LNA, a noise canceling structure and an active inductor were employed to reduce noise figure and to realize input matching and gain tuning respectively. At the middle stage, three common-emitter amplifier was utilized to realize high gain. Furthermore, current reuse technique is used at input stage and middle stage respectively to reduce power consumption. At the output stage, an emitter follower was adopted to achieve output matching. Based on WIN 0.2μm GaAs HBT technology, the proposed LPVG-LNA was verified. The results show that in the frequency range of 1-3GHz, the LPVG-LNA has the gain (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub>) of over 37.56dB, the maximum gain tuning range of 4.22dB, the input return loss (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>) of less than -7.06dB, the output return loss (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</sub>) of less than -18.52dB, the noise figure (NF) of less than 4.6dB, the stability factor (k) of over 10.68. The static power dissipation of the LPVG-LNA is less than 35mW under the operation voltage of 5V.

articleTitle: Research on adaptive burst delay algorithm of laser fuze
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: The kill probability of missile to target can be effectively improved by adaptive burst delay control technique. In this paper, a typical air target was taken as an example. The simulation of the Monte Carlo statistical test was carried out by Coordination of Fuze and Worhead (CFAW) software. Genetic Simulated Annealing (GSA) hybrid algorithm was used to fit the statistical experimental results. The adaptive burst delay control model of engineering available was obtained.

articleTitle: ADI-FDTD method in layered breast model scattering analysis for microwave tomography
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: The conventional FDTD method is extensively applied in dealing with microwave imaging, however, because of the constraint of Courant-Friedrich-Levy (CFL) stability condition, the time-step size required should be smaller enough as well as the fine cells selected is smaller, which brings an increase computational effort. The ADI-FDTD method, on the other hand, utilizing alternating-direction implicit method is available to overcome the constraint of Courant-Friedrich-Levy (CFL) stability condition. It is obvious that the processing result of ADI-FDTD method and conventional FDTD method can coincide with each other perfectly by the MATLAB simulation experiment.

articleTitle: Outage analysis on wireless powered cooperative systems with spatially random relays and finite energy storage over Rayleigh fading channels
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper investigates the outage performance of a cooperative system with spatially random wireless powered relays and finite energy storage over Rayleigh fading channels. In the considered system, a destination (D) and a source (S) are both equipped with one transmit antenna to transmit power and information to relays, respectively. Meanwhile, relay candidates with one transmit antenna are spatially random distributed in a disc, the central of which the source locates in. A best relay (R) with the best source-relay link is selected to forward the decoded information to D. Further, D and all relay candidates are equipped N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</sub> (N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</sub> ≥ 1) with N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</sub> (N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sub> ≥ 1) receiving antennas and adopt maximal ratio combining scheme to process multiple received signals. The closed-form analytical expression for the outage probability is derived while considering relays are with finite energy storage. Simulations are conducted to validate the accuracy of our analysis.

Author Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer

articleTitle: Multichannel energy detection UWB receivers based on nonlinear square law technology
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, a multichannel energy detection (MED) receiver based on nonlinear square law (SL) technology is proposed for ultra-wideband (UWB) system. By using a group of band-pass filters, the received signal processed by SL device is separated into multiple channels, and then the channel with serious narrow band interference (NBI) will be omitted to improve the NBI mitigation ability of the receiver. Simulation results show that comparing with conventional ED receivers, the proposed SL-MED receiver can significantly improve the bit-error-rate performance when one or two NBIs are present and even no NBI presents.

articleTitle: Hierarchical visible light communication system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Visible light communication (VLC) has attached a lot of interests due to its safety, practicability, and efficiency. In a VLC system with multiple light-emitting-diodes (LEDs), two different types of channels named imaging channel and non-imaging channel can be used to transmit data. In this paper, basing on the channel characteristics, we propose a novel hierarchical VLC system which supports two different types of receivers simultaneously. Meanwhile, we also demonstrate how to achieve maximum throughput with optimal power allocation. Numerical results are also provided to corroborate our designs.

articleTitle: A low-profile top-loaded folded helical antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile folded helical antenna with a top hat loading. It consists of two identical normal mode helices mounted on a large ground plane and a square conducting plate on the top of them to achieve a low profile. One helix is fed by a coaxial probe while the other one is connected to the ground, forming a folding structure for high resonant resistance. Parametric study is conducted to show the effect of the size of the top hat and the helix on the antenna's resonance character. A prototype is fabricated and tested, measured results show that an impedance bandwidth of 8% is achieved with an antenna height of 0.08λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (λ0 is the free-space wavelength at its center operating frequency).

articleTitle: A novel dual-frequency phase inverter
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this letter, a novel dual-frequency phase inverter is proposed. The interdigital striplines and metallic vias are used to obtain 180 degree phase shift. The different length of the slotlines in the ground can obtain different operation frequencies. The structure of the phase inverter is simple and can be realized with ordinary microwave integrated circuit (MIC) fabrication process. The two simulations show the phase inverter can work at two different frequencies.

articleTitle: Analysis of channel rate in single-user massive MIMO systems with IQ imbalances at UE
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, we consider single-cell massive multiple-input multiple output (MIMO) systems with in-phase and quadrature-phase imbalances (IQI) at the user equipment (UE). We investigate the effect of IQI on the channel rate. The upper bound and the lower bound are derived. Results show that both the upper and the lower bound are limited by IQI as the number of the antennas grows large for a single user system. And the channel estimation error has non-zero floor if IQI exists.

articleTitle: The analysis and implementation of millimeter-wave LFMCW fuse
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper presents a scheme about the proximity fuse based on LFMCW ranging radar and studies the parameter design requirements, the signal quality, the accuracy and the stability of the fuse in different terrain. Echo signal quality, ranging accuracy and stability of different terrain and different illumination angles are studied through experimental verification.

articleTitle: Noise-reducing architecture of compressed sensing receiver for IR-UWB ranging systems
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A compressed sensing (CS) based impulse radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) receiver with two-path noise-reducing RF front-end architecture is proposed. By adding an identical input path (antenna and gain stage) together with a mixer, the noise in the received signal before feeding into the CS sampling block is alleviated comparing with the conventional CS receiver. Moreover, the mixing stage shifts the signal frequency spectrum to the lower band which eases the CS sampling hardware as well as the complexity of back-end signal reconstruction. Simulation results for a ranging system validate that the proposed CS receiver significantly outperforms the conventional one in both additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel and IEEE 802.15.4a multi-path channel.

articleTitle: Joint data recovery and NBI mitigation in OFDM systems using CS framework
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, a novel approach is proposed to jointly recover the transmitted data and mitigate narrow-band interference (NBI) in OFDM systems using compressive sensing (CS) framework. NBI degrades the performance of OFDM systems which motivates the need for mitigation techniques to reduce its effect. The main idea behind our approach is to represent the transmitted data and the NBI signal as a sparse vector and then solve a joint optimization problem. Therefore, the modulated signal using popular modulation schemes such as BPSK, QPSK, and M-PAM is represented by binary representation using some dictionaries. NBI is a sparse signal in the frequency domain, however, frequency-grid-mismatch destroys the sparsity of NBI at the receiver. We propose a structured-dictionary-mismatch formulation to estimate the frequency-grid-mismatch and recover the sparsity of the NBI in the frequency domain. The optimization problem is formulated as a combined re-weighted ℓ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> and ℓ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,1</sub> norms. The solution aims to recover the transmitted data and NBI jointly.

articleTitle: A novel low-profile broadband circularly polarized compact antenna array
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A novel low-profile broadband circularly polarized compact 2×2 array is presented in this paper. The array combines the advantages of stacked patch structure, sequential-rotation method and a feed network composed of Wilkinson power divider and T-junction power splitter, exhibiting excellent performance. The dual feeds of the square patch are connected to output ports of Wilkinson power divider with a 90° phase shifter to radiate circularly polarized wave. Then, a compact 2×2 array fed by sequential-rotation method to form phase 0°, −90°, −180° and −270° is proposed, with a low profile less than 0.1 wavelength. All of the radiation elements and feed network are printed on the lower substrate without the need of a separate substrate for feed network, while four parasitic patches are printed on the upper substrate. Experimental results show that the array can achieve an impedance bandwidth of 27.78% for the 10-dB return loss and a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 52%. The antenna gain bandwidth, considering 1-dB gain variation within the impedance bandwidth, is about 16%, with the maximum gain about 14.19dBi.

articleTitle: Design of RCS measurement system RF front-end hardware circuit based on L band
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: As the core part and the key link of RCS measurement system, the design and optimization of RF front-end circuit is of great significance. According to an existing 2GHz-18GHz outdoor RCS measurement system, the RF front-end of the system based on L band is designed from the system level to extend the frequency band of the system. The hardware circuit consists of the transmitting and receiving circuits as well as the IF processing unit, and it is achieved by the mixer solution. The filter circuit as well as other components of the system are designed and simulated by ADS software. From selecting the RF amplifiers and other chips used in the system to drawing schematic and PCB layout by using Altium Designer, and then welding components, debugging related hardware and measuring related parameter, the measurement system hardware circuit design is completed systematically.

articleTitle: A novel wideband bandpass filter using cross-shaped slotline structure
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A novel wideband bandpass filter (BPF) using cross-shaped slotline is presented in this paper. It can achieve wideband response from 7.96 GHz to 12.18 GHz with three poles at 8.37 GHz, 9.95 GHz, 11.64 GHz and four zeros at 5.4 GHz, 5.76 GHz, 13.36 GHz and 14.07 GHz with slotline. Compared with terminated cross-shaped resonators (CSRs) with short circuit terminations, this CSR slotline filter is relax from via implantation with similar wideband response. And measured results show the filter has a good performance.

articleTitle: “Available seat?” — Case analysis of interactive device and interactive design project
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper analyzes the case creative used interactive techniques and design. This paper expatiates on the means, the methods and the essence of interactive design on new media art in public space, which through the creative concepts, the function of interactive system; and also realize ideas, technical system design and analysis, and the significance of experiments and application value, which are in the field of human-computer interaction in public spaces.

articleTitle: An efficient numerical technique to calculate the electromagnetic scattering from the convex scatters
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: High frequency electromagnetic (EM) scattering analysis of electrically large objects is of great interest for engineering applications. It is noted that computation effort of the scattering fields using the uniform geometrical theory of diffraction (UTD) is simple and efficient. This high frequency approximating method requires values for the TM/TE Pekeris-integral functions. Here, the integrals are evaluated by using of a simple extension of a Fourier quadrature method which is related to the discrete Fourier transform. Compared to the exact Eigen-function solution, the procedure derived by Pearson is believed to be efficient for computing fields scattered by an impedance cylinder.

articleTitle: An investigation for the parameters of the inverted cavity-backed slot antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, an investigation for the parameters of the inverted cavity-backed slot (ICBS) antenna is proposed. Typical numerical results are presented to show the effect of various cavity size, slot dimensions and feedline on impedance of the antenna. In addition, the design size of cavity, slot and feed line is suggested, which can be seen as design guidelines of the ICBS antenna.

articleTitle: A co-aperture planar antenna for CDMA/GPS/Zigbee applications
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, a novel compact planar antenna using the co-aperture concept is presented for CDMA/GPS/Zigbee applications. By simultaneously placing three antennas with different shapes and polarization directions in a small place and considering the coupling among them, the co-aperture with three ports and good in-band performance could be designed on a small PCB. In order to validate this design, the proposed antenna is simulated by HFSS simulator. The simulation shows that this antenna operates at three frequency bands (CDMA/GPS/Zigbee) with high gain of above 2 dBi and high isolations among input ports of above 28 dB within its impedance bandwidth, and the polarization direction of the GPS band is circular. Considering the three ports and small dimensions of 106.5 mm × 66 mm × 1.6 mm, it can be treated as an antenna-triplexer directly used in the hand-held terminals for both communication and positioning.

articleTitle: Null steering based on space mapping method for large-scale arrays
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In the paper, the technique for antenna array pattern beamforming with null steering is presented. This technique deals with the possibilities to cancel undesired interferences by steering nulls of the pattern in the direction of high interference without affecting the main beam. Based on the null steering technique, the sidelobe level of the array antenna pattern can be maintained. Furthermore, the domain decomposition method based on the equivalence principle algorithm and space mapping method is applied to analyze and optimize large scale array antennas. Numerical results show the efficiency of the proposed technique for array optimizations.

articleTitle: Performance of finite-resolution receivers for M-QAM systems with IQ imbalances
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In the paper, we concentrate on investigating the effect of imbalances between In-phase(I) and Quadrature-phase(Q) branches in high-order quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) systems with finite resolution. We find that the zero intermediate frequency (zero-IF) receiver can't handle the IQ imbalances even with the full resolution (FR) when the order of QAM is pretty high, e.g. 64, 256. Instead, the digital intermediate frequency (digital-IF) receiver can provide an acceptable performance.

articleTitle: A fast matrix pencil method in non-uniform sampling scheme for discrete complex image methods
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Discrete complex image methods are of closed form methods for fast calculating Green's functions of stratified media, which have been widely discussed by many researchers. In the present paper, one fast non-uniform sampling matrix pencil method is proposed to improve the efficiency of discrete complex image methods. One numerical example and some comparisons are also provided, where a sampling scheme of two-segment is used in the proposed method, which validate its accuracy and improvement.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a dual-circular polarization reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: The two-layer dual-Circular Polarization (CP) reflectarray antenna has been designed in this paper. The upper element structure is based on CP selective surfaces (CPSS) for LCP and the second layer adopts reactively loaded ring slots for RCP. Finally, a 20-cm two-layer reflectarray antenna has been designed and simulated for verification. A good agreement with the corresponding single layer demonstrates that it could operate in dual CP communications with high isolation. The compact structure, low cost and ease of fabrication make this reflectarray more required in space application.

articleTitle: Research on electromagnetic parameters of superconductors in a wide range of operating temperatures and frequencies
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Based on the Mattis-Bardeen equations, the contour maps for complex conductivity, bulk surface impedance and conductivity quality factor of a classical superconducting material (aluminum) are calculated with the temperature ranging from 0 K to 1.2K (the transition temperature, Tc), and the frequency ranging from 1 GHz to 162 GHz (twice gap frequency). It is shown that the microwave properties of superconducting materials are mainly determined by temperature when the operating frequency is below the gap frequency. Also, it is found that the surface impedance is near a pure reactance in the range [0, 0.25Tc], and the quality factor is more than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> in the range [0, 0.1Tc].

articleTitle: Design of low phase noise and area-efficient PLL in microwave generation and intelligent control
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: An integer-N phase-locked loop (PLL) is designed and fabricated in TSMC 0.18-um CMOS technology. The proposed PLL with a complementary crossed-couple LC-tank voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) and a mixed design of current mode logic (CML) and true single phase clock (TSPC) logic in the frequency divider achieves a fiber lasers application in microwave signal generation and intelligent computing from a free running mode-locked Er-fiber laser. In the stretched-pulse regime, the Er-fiber laser is designed at close-to-zero dispersion to minimize the phase noise of extracted microwaves. In order to suppress the excess phase noise in the optical to electronic conversion process, we synchronize a low-noise PLL to the fiber laser using a fiber Sagnac-loop-based optical-microwave phase detector.

articleTitle: Design of single-channel angle tracking receiver for V band
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A V-band single-channel angle tracking receiver is developed in this paper, which consists of a 60GHz single-channel modulator module and a V-band down conversion channel. The design of V-band down conversion channel aims at high integration, miniaturization and engineering design. Multiple frequency components and harmonics wave are calculated, avoided and suppressed in the realization of conversion of V band to low frequency and ensure a good channel performance. Experiment results show that noise figure of the 60GHz single-channel modulator is less than 5dB and the gain is greater than 32dB within the bandwidth of 3GHz; Output power of V-band down conversion channel in 1dB compression point is greater than 8dBm; output power in AGC mode is 5dBm;clutter suppression is more than 60dBc and harmonic suppression is more than 40dBc.

articleTitle: Power allocation game for wireless network localization
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Power allocation is critical for location-aware networks, since transmitting power greatly affects localization accuracy and determines the lifetime of wireless networks. In this paper, we formulate a game-theoretic power allocation scheme for anchors that can achieve a desirable trade-off between power consumption and localization accuracy. We derive the closed form expression for the best response strategy of each anchor in the single agent scenario, and prove the existence of Nash Equilibrium (NE). We further propose a distributed algorithm to implement our proposed scheme. Numerical results show that our scheme can guarantee a given accuracy with a higher energy efficiency, comparing to the exhaustive scheme.

articleTitle: A low-profile broadband planar antenna for super thin portable wireless devices
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this article, an inverted-F antenna with parasitic element is proposed. The antenna is composed of an inverted-F element which is consist of two branches, a parasitic element, and a ground plate, where these lie in the same plane of the subplate. The size of the proposed antenna is 59mm in length and 10mm in width which bandwidths can cover the global system for mobile communication (880-960MHz), digital communication system (1710-1880MHz), personal communication system (1850-1990mhZ), and universal mobile telecommunication system (1920-2170MHz) bands for the criterion of VSWR = 3. The antenna is suitable for wireless handsets or some other mobile wireless communication devices. Details of the proposed design, and simulation and measurement results are presented.

articleTitle: FG-FFT method using higher order basis functions for solving EM scattering problems
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper states that Fitting Green's function Fast Fourier Transformation (FG-FFT) algorithm applies to accelerating matrix vector product of higher order Method of Moments (MoM). For different patch, the local expansion box is employed with the same expansion order of every Gaussian point. Combined the high accuracy of the FG-FFT with this scheme, it makes the FG-FFT very suitable for high order basis function. Therefore, comparing other the FFT-based methods, higher order FG-FFT algorithm is more effective. The numerical examples presented in this paper show that the high order FG-FFT is more accuracy and efficiency for electrically large object.

articleTitle: Measurement fusion of connectivity and received signal strength for indoor localization and tracking
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: The range-free localization suffers from unstable connectivity information between wireless devices. To overcome this, we propose a Markov Chain Monte Carlo particle filter (MCMC PF)-based mobility tracking algorithm assisted by received signal strength (RSS) information. The range-free localization results and RSS measurements are used in the tracking algorithm. From MATLAB simulation, we confirm the performance of the proposed tracking algorithm compensating the defect of the range-free localization, and the efficient indoor mobility tracking in a realistic indoor environment has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: An error beacon filtering algorithm based on particle swarm optimization for underwater wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Due to the sophisticated environmental variations of water current, underwater creature touch, and strong electromagnetic interference, some beacon nodes tend to move or be damaged, which thus results in larger positioning errors of ordinary nodes. In order to solve the error beacon problem, this paper proposes an error beacon filtering algorithm based on particle swarm optimization (PSO), which can differentiate the beacon accurately. Firstly, several location errors of beacons are calculated by an improved Trilateration, and then the beacon with the maximum positioning error is filtered out through PSO. The remaining beacons are filtered out consecutively until the location error of each beacon does not exceed a preset threshold. Simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm can detect almost all error beacons effectively with smaller variances.

articleTitle: Multiple arcs based image extrapolation method for millimeter wave UWB radar
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Range points migration (RPM) method is a successful 3-D imaging algorithm with higher accuracy and less computational cost. Due to the limitation of radar aperture size, usually, the boundary points estimated by RPM method only cover a small portion of target surface. Therefore image extrapolation method is needed for improving the image result of RPM method. The conventional image extrapolation method is established based on ellipsoid fitting. However, such a high freedom optimization problem leads to extremely high computational cost. In order to accelerate the computation, we propose a novel image extrapolation method for based on multiple arcs. In the proposed method, instead of ellipsoids, a group of arcs are estimated to describe the targets. In this way, original 3-D problem is degenerated to a 2-D one, which contributes a significant reduction of computational cost. The numerical simulation results show that the proposed method can realize image extrapolation in success with significantly higher accuracy and computational speed.

articleTitle: Technique of interference prediction in cognitive radio based on suffix array
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: By analyzing the law of the usage of historical spectrum data, spectrum prediction can be used to predict the future usage state of the spectrum. This technology can be taken to predict the jamming signal in communication countermeasure. In order to achieve the reliable forecast of the jamming signal in the artificial interference channel environment (a channel with the man-made interference), this paper proposes a spectrum prediction algorithm based on suffix array, which could guide the cognitive users to switch between spectrums autonomously. Moreover, a cognitive radio system is built to verify the algorithm. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm predicts well with the small sampled historical spectrum data.

articleTitle: PU state-based sequential cooperative spectrum sensing algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A PU (Primary User) State-based Sequential Cooperative Spectrum Sensing (PSSCSS) algorithm was presented which based on the occupation characteristics of authorized channel and sequential spectrum sensing. The duration of PU's presence or absence in authorized channel is far greater than sensing period. Cognitive nodes perform different sequential spectrum sensing according to the sensing result of last time to improve the performance and efficiency of the system. The simulation results show that compared to the hard combination, soft combination and non PU state-based sequential cooperative spectrum sensing algorithm, this algorithm can greatly improves detection performance by smaller transmission bandwidth at the expense of little increase in time consumption.

articleTitle: Influence of I-Doser stimulation on brain waves activity at different frequencies
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, the influence of I-Doser stimulation on brain waves activity at different frequencies is investigated. Researches on the perception mechanism of brain waves, including alpha-wave, beta-wave, theta-wave, and delta-wave, and the relevant pattern of the spectral power have been done. Three popular online audio samples and one self-made sample are used to in the test, the testees listen to those I-Dosers with various speeds and frequencies. As a result of our experiments, we concluded that the alpha-wave is of the most sensitive to the speed change and being active in the initial while being inactive lately. The beta-wave is easiest produce mandatory memory of the high frequency audio and can generate brain physiology reaction. Moreover, the theta-wave can react to the persistent low frequency audio and the delta-wave has the sensitivity of frequency response that is closely related to the music professional quality of the testees.

articleTitle: Study of S-band antenna tracking algorithm based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Most conventional antenna tracking algorithm in the DSP implementation, often require a separate DSP or CPU hardware units. The aerospace applications in order to meet the miniaturization, low power requirements, based on the communication signal processing on FPGA antenna tracking algorithm, additional antenna tracking computing unit is not required. Coordinate changes and solving the beam steering angle of operation of the algorithm involved in ensuring the accuracy to meet the engineering requirements of the premise, using a look-up table, multiplier and CORDIC algorithm structure of pipe-line contour integration, low hardware cost method to calculate the beam steering-angle.

articleTitle: Design of the 60 GHz transceiver front end for high speed data transmission system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Compared with the existing communication system, 60 GHz technology has many advantages. This paper introduced the design of the 60 GHz transceiver front end for high speed data transmission system, and discussed the realization method of some key high frequency components, such as V band low noise amplifier, V band modulator and so on. The output power of the transmitter is +3dBm, the error vector magnitude (EVM) is less than 8%; the receiver gain is greater than 50dB, the output power of 1dB compression point is greater than 10dBm, the noise figure is less than 5dB. System experiment shows that the quality of the modulated signal generated by the transmitter is good, and the degeneration caused by the receiver is small, which means that our transceiver front end can meet the requirements of the 0.9Gbps data transmission system.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave massive-MIMO channel sounding for future mobile broadband
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: Achieving the foreseeable high bandwidth and high data rate required for over 100 billion estimated data hungry devices in 2020 and beyond is the major goal of 5G technology. The synergy between millimeter-wave and massive MIMO technology in mobile communication will enhance the actualization of 5G systems. However, Channel behavior is not well understood for wireless multiple-access communications at millimeter wave band. Channel sounding is therefore needed to characterized future potential 5G air interface. 5G Channel sounding system must meet up with three fundamental requirements: Ultra-band wideband; millimeter-wave frequency band; and massive MIMO. In this paper, these requirements were verified via simulation. These basic requirements make 5G channel sounding systems highly challenging. Series of problems and various ways of addressing them for adequate and efficient channel characterization were highlighted. Keysight's Agilent SystemVue and Matlab softwares were identified as useful tools for electronic system level design and simulation of 5G channel sounder.

articleTitle: Miniaturized balanced bandpass filter using dual-mode dielectric resonator
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper introduces, for the first time, a balanced dual-mode bandpass filter (BPF) using a compact rectangular dielectric resonator (DR), which is directly contact with the bottom of the metal cavity. The idea is to use the bottom metal plate of the cavity to replace the electric wall of the dominant modes, i.e., TE<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sup><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> and TE<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sup><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>, which are orthogonal to each other, of the rectangular DR, so as to keep the half field distributions of the two modes unaffected and the size of the DR becomes nearly half of the conventional one. The two half-cut modes can be used for constructing the differential-mode (DM) passband of a balanced dual-mode BPF. For demonstration, a balanced dual-mode BPF employing the proposed rectangular DR is designed and simulated, showing good DM and common-mode (CM) responses and offering a significant size reduction in comparison with the conventional DR filters.

articleTitle: Design of an improved short-circuited stub ultra-wideband bandpass filter based on LTCC
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, a method of designing an improved ultra-wideband LTCC bandpass filter is proposed from the 3 orders bandpass filter of parallel short-circuited stub, and it includes three basic cells: coupled connecting line, parallel short-circuited stub and parallel short-circuited coupled line. The addition of coupled connecting line improve the pass-band performance and the edge steep characteristic. Utilizing the zeros properties of parallel short-circuited coupled line, two transmission zeros are produced at the up and below sides. At last, the passband of filter is 3.1 ~ 11.6GHz, insert loss is less than 1.5dB, and the stopband rejection is nearly 30dB (0~2.4GHz, 11.8~15GHz). The dimension of the filter is only 5mm × 3.6mm × 1.5mm.

articleTitle: A wideband bandpass filter based on interdigital couplers
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A novel wideband bandpass filter based on interdigital couplers is proposed and implemented using a multiple-mode resonator (MMR). In the design, the interdigital coupling is used to form the resonator of low impedance. The first three resonant frequencies of this MMR are properly adjusted to be placed quasi equally within the passband. The interdigital lines at the two sides are deployed so as to raise the frequency-dispersive coupling degree. The cross structure in the center is used to form high impedance resonator. After the optimization of this filter, a good wideband bandpass behavior is theoretically realized and experimentally confirmed.

articleTitle: Design of a broadband cross-shaped patch antenna for phased array
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In this paper, a wide bandwidth, wide-angle patch antenna with acceptable circular polarization performance is presented. The antenna combines the advantages of capacitance coupling feed, backed cavity and a feed network based on Wilkinson power divider, exhibiting an excellent performance. When the antenna is located in an array, it shows low-level mutual coupling and broader beamwidth. The characteristics make the antenna an ideal choice for phased array. Both simulated and measured results demonstrate that the antenna can achieve a wide bandwidth of 110° with 28% bandwidth and for S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub><;-10dB with 30% bandwidth.

articleTitle: Design of the high-performance RF transmitter for IEEE 802.11ac system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In the field of high-speed wireless LAN, IEEE 802.11ac is gradually becoming the mainstream standard. Based on the main requirements of IEEE 802.11ac standard, this paper provides details on how to implement the high performance RF transmitter working in 5GHz to 6GHz band, which can support the very high throughput (VHT) mode of the standard. The maxim bandwidth of the transmitter is 80MHz and 256-QAM modulation is supported. The transmitter uses double-conversion super-heterodyne structure, in which the intermediate frequency (IF) is selected at 1.05GHz, with an 80MHz bandwidth. The test results show that the maximum output power is up to 18dBm and for every working frequency, the gain flatness is less than 0.5dB. The modulation accuracies evaluated by error vector magnitude (EVM) of the 10MHz and 80MHz bandwidth signals with 256-QAM modulation are better than 0.6% and 0.9%. When 80MHz bandwidth IEEE 801.11ac signal with 256-QAM modulation is applied to the transmitter system, the EVM is below -40dB when the output power is lower than 10dBm.

articleTitle: A 0.775mW 10-bit 40-MS/s SAR ADC in 0.18μm CMOS process
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper presents the design of 10-bit, 40-MS/s successive approximation register (SAR) analog-to-digital converter (ADC). A new asynchronous control structure is proposed. To reduce the power consumption, the monotonic capacitor switching procedure is used. To enhance the linearity of ADC, a two-phase non-overlapping clock is used. In order to improve the speed of comparison, redundant MOS transistor is added to the comparator. The prototype was implemented in 0.18pm 1P6M CMOS process. Under a 1.8-V supply and a 40-MS/s sampling rate, the power consumption of SAR ADC is only 0.775mW.

articleTitle: Theoretical research and ADS simulation of tunable band-pass filter
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: In RF transceiver system, it is necessary to add a tunable band-pass filter in the system to solve the problem of frequency congestion and improve the system's anti-interference performance. The circuit structure with a continuous tunability for both the resonant frequency and bandwidth which is constant is presented theoretically in this paper, the resonance circuit is viewed as a resistance at the resonant frequency, T inductance coupling is adopted, ADS is used to simulate and verify. The simulation results show that the center frequency varies from 66 MHz to 72 MHz while the resonant capacitance changes from 60 pF to 50 pF and bandwidth keeps 5 MHz, the bandwidth reduces from 5 MHz to 3.5 MHz when the coupled inductance decreases from 58.186 nH to 40.532 nH, the filtering performance is good at the tuning frequency point, the insertion loss increases about 0.223 dB when tuning the bandwidth and it slightly reduces the system performance but meets the requirements of RF communication, the filter's analyses in the paper provides a theoretical basis for the practical production.

articleTitle: Periordic leaky-wave antenna based on substrate integrated nonradiative dielectric waveguide
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: The air via-hole array makes it possible that a periordic leaky-wave antenna is fabricated in the substrate integrated nonradiative dielectric (SINRD) waveguide. The distances between the via-holes have an enormous influence on the design of a leaky-wave antenna and the leakage loss of SINRD structures. In this paper, the coplanar waveguide (CPW) is used to stimulate the SINRD waveguide through the triangle transition in order to produce the leaky-wave antenna mode and the design of this transition is studied. The characteristics of the proposed periodic leaky-wave antenna under the leaky-wave mode are analyzed. Based on the SINRD waveguide, simple design rules are provided and discussed. Moreover, the simulation results have verified the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Design of a one-dimensional wideband and wide scanning phased array antenna
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper presents an improved phased array antenna which is based on the Vivaldi antenna. This phased array antenna has good UWB (ultra-wide bandwidth) characteristics. Meanwhile, its scanning angle has reached to 60 degrees. The length of each radiation unit has been optimized under the application of the low sidelobe algorithm, for the purpose of weakening the sidelobe. By the one-dimensional arrangement of radiation units, the gain of this antenna is highly improved. A sort of exponential tapered microstrip line is applied in the antenna design while several metal boards are used to reduce mutual coupling among these radiating units.

articleTitle: Design of a high-efficiency Doherty GaN power amplifier
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: An S-band power amplifier (PA)was designed with a three-stage cascade structure in this paper. To achieve high efficiency up to 6 dB output power back-off (OPBO) and high linearity, GaN devices of high gain and efficiency were chosen for the driver amplifier, Doherty power amplifier (DPA) based on CREE CGH40025 was designed for the last stage amplifier. GaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) have attracted great attention because of the outstanding material properties and an excellent trade-of between output power and efficiency, the research of the DPA based on GaN devices has become a hotspot. The DPA was designed to achieve high average efficiency for digitally modulated signals with high peak to average power ratio (PAR) used in mobile and satellite communication system. The PA provides peak output power of 47.22dBm, gain of 43dB and 64% power added efficiency (PAE). It exhibits a PAE of 38% at 6dB output power back-off and -21.5 dBc IM3 at 3dB output power back-off. The measured results show that Doherty amplifiers have high efficiency and good linearity to solve the problem on linearity and efficiency of the RF power amplifiers.

articleTitle: On sequential blind channel estimation for time-varying OFDM system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: A new algorithm is proposed for the sequential blind channel estimation of the Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) systems. Different from other blind algorithms which carry out estimation for a fixed set of subchannels or time-slots, the new algorithm based on the Expectation-Maximization (EM) method is offered to obtain the Maximum-likelihood (ML) estimation of the time-domain channel impulse response (CIR) sequentially. We also propose a novel recursive approach to get the parameter value. This recursive approach not only reduces computing complexity but also avoids computing instability. It's further shown that this algorithm can be simplified mathematically by combining iteration and recursion. Simulations illustrate these algorithms provide better performance than other algorithms.

articleTitle: Source localization using TDOA measurements with sensor position errors
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Ubiquitous Wireless Broadband (ICUWB)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved two-step weighted least squares (TSWLS) algorithm for target location using time difference of arrival (TDOA) with sensor position errors. The performance of the TSWLS method is improved in a simple way through re-selecting reference sensor and rotating co-ordinate system, and the improved TSWLS(I-TSWLS) algorithm remains to be closed-form and approximately efficient as the TSWLS method. Simulation results show that the I-TSWLS algorithm can achieve the CRLB easily before higher noise threshold, and it exhibits lower estimation bias and better robustness with increasing sensor position errors.
